title: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Calls for ‘Team Agriculture’ to Make India a Global Food Basket
subtitle:
Centre, States Must Rise Above Politics to Put Farmers First: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

India’s Farm Produce Set to Gain Global Reach Through New Trade Opportunities: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan

More than ₹1200 Crore PM-RKVY Support Sanctioned to 10 States at National Agriculture Conference

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Announces Stronger Centre-State Coordination and Nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’

Natural Farming, Integrated Agriculture and Crop Diversification Key to a More Sustainable Farm Sector: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 2:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
On the second day of the National Agriculture Conference – Rabi Campaign 2026, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired a session attended by Agriculture Ministers and senior officials from various states. Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said that under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Centre and states must rise above party politics and work in the spirit of ‘Team Agriculture’ to ensure the country’s food security and improve farmers’ livelihoods. “Governments and political parties come and go; parties are formed and dissolved, but the country and its farmers are eternal,” he said, stressing that the platform was not about politics but about finding practical ways to improve agriculture and advance the interests of farmers. Shri Chouhan also highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, farmers’ interests have been accorded the highest priority in every major policy decision and international agreement. At the conference, Shri Chouhan handed over financial sanction letters worth more than ₹1200 crore to Agriculture Ministers of 10 states under the Prime Minister Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY). Union Ministers of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur and Shri Bhagirath Choudhary, Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra, ICAR Director General Dr. M. L. Jat, along with senior officials from the Centre and states, scientists and representatives of various agricultural institutions, were present at the conference.
More than ₹ 1200 crore sanctioned to 10 states under PM-RKVY
Under PM-RKVY, sanction letters were distributed to 10 states, including ₹290 crore for West Bengal, ₹198 crore for Haryana, ₹181 crore for Chhattisgarh, ₹154 crore for Arunachal Pradesh, ₹114 crore for Bihar, ₹104 crore for Karnataka, ₹75 crore for Mizoram, ₹64 crore for Himachal Pradesh, ₹58 crore for Jharkhand and ₹43 crore for Punjab.
Shri Chouhan said the Union Government was not limiting itself to policy formulation, but was also ensuring timely availability of resources to states so that implementation of schemes could begin on the ground without delay.
Agriculture growth rate rises to 4.5 per cent
Highlighting the country’s agricultural performance, Shri Chouhan said that since 2015, the agriculture growth rate has increased from 3 per cent to 4.5 per cent. The average annual increase in foodgrain production has also more than doubled, rising from around 40 lakh tonnes earlier to 84 lakh tonnes per year. He further noted that in just two years, from 2023-24 to 2025-26, rabi foodgrain production recorded an unprecedented increase of 205 lakh tonnes. He attributed this historic growth to the collective efforts of state agriculture departments, scientists and farmers.
Monthly virtual reviews with states to strengthen cooperative federalism
Announcing a new mechanism to further strengthen cooperative federalism, Shri Chouhan said that, on the lines of weekly reviews conducted at the Centre, regular monthly virtual review meetings with states would now be held to continuously assess progress. At the state level, a strong State Agriculture Team will be constituted by bringing together the Agriculture Minister, Agriculture Secretary, state agricultural universities, ICAR institutions, Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ATMA, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), progressive farmers, processors, exporters and nodal officers of the Government of India. At the district level, monthly meetings will be held involving the Collector, Deputy Director of Agriculture (DDA), ATMA, KVKs, ICAR scientists, bankers and farmers.
Annual calendar for pre-season agriculture interface meetings
To ensure advance preparation for agricultural campaigns, Shri Chouhan announced an annual calendar for interface meetings. For the Kharif campaign, district-level meetings will be held on May 10 and state-level meetings on May 17 every year. Similarly, for the Rabi campaign, district-level meetings will be held on September 10 and state-level meetings on September 17 every year. In addition, a one-day special meeting will be organised across the country on a common date, bringing together Agriculture Ministers, officials and agricultural scientists simultaneously to discuss issues concerning farmers.
‘
Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30
Emphasising the need to protect soil health and the environment, Shri Chouhan called for a nationwide ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan’ from October 22 to November 30 this year. Scientists and all key stakeholders will actively participate in the campaign. Based on Soil Health Cards, the campaign will promote balanced use of fertilisers to protect soil fertility and beneficial insects. He also called for large-scale promotion of pulse cultivation in rice fallow areas of eastern India, particularly in Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal, after the paddy harvest.
Rabi preparations to focus on soil moisture, water availability and crop protection
As part of preparations for the current rabi season, Shri Chouhan stressed that recommendations on crops and improved seeds should be based on soil moisture and water availability. He directed states to put in place effective arrangements to protect crops from diseases and pests, ensure saturation of all eligible farmers with Kisan Credit Cards (KCCs) and conduct transparent Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) under the crop insurance scheme. He also emphasised that state ministers should personally undertake regular reviews of the implementation of departmental schemes.
Strict action against spurious inputs, end to forced tagging
Stating that the availability of seeds and fertilisers in the country is adequate, Shri Chouhan directed states to take strict legal action against fake fertilisers, spurious seeds and sub-standard pesticides. He also directed that forced tagging be completely eliminated. Calling for agriculture to become more sustainable and remunerative, he urged states to adopt natural farming, integrated farming systems and crop diversification in mission mode.
Government working on multi-pronged strategy to ensure remunerative prices for farmers
Shri Chouhan said the government is pursuing a multi-dimensional strategy to ensure that farmers receive fair and remunerative prices for their produce. The strategy includes strengthening post-harvest management, scientific warehousing and marketing systems. He said that 100 per cent assured government procurement of tur, urad and masoor at MSP would be undertaken, with arrangements for payment within 48 hours. In line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, he said India would also leverage the new market opportunities emerging from international Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to connect Indian agricultural products, fruits, vegetables and foodgrains with global markets. This, he said, would help farmers secure better returns for their produce and enable India to emerge as a major ‘food basket’ for the world.

title: Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu curtain-raises Routes Asia
subtitle: 23rd Routes Asia to be held from 16-18 March 2027 in New Delhi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu
today unveiled the Curtain Raiser for Routes Asia 2027 in New Delhi, marking a significant milestone in India's preparations to host the prestigious international aviation event. The Curtain Raiser witnessed participation from representatives of 28 embassies, along with leading aviation stakeholders, underscoring the growing international engagement and collaborative opportunities surrounding Routes Asia 2027.
The 24
th
edition of Routes Asia will be held from 16–18 March 2027 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, bringing together more than 115 leading airlines, representatives from 55+ countries, airports, tourism authorities and aviation stakeholders from across Asia and beyond.
Minister of Civil Aviation, Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu
, while unveiling the curtain raiser plaque, presented India's vision for Routes Asia 2027 under the theme “Bharat Aviation Rising: Inclusive Growth – Connecting Asia & Beyond.” He highlighted that guided by the vision of
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
, the event comes at an opportune moment as India advances towards becoming the world's third-largest aviation market.
He said, “Routes Asia 2027 is coming to the right place, at the right time, with the right opportunity! There is room for more capacity, more airlines and more routes”.
With over 166 airports and plans to develop 100 additional airports over the next decade, India's aviation sector is witnessing rapid expansion. The Minister emphasised the growing importance of the hub-and-spoke model, which can connect more cities and people with emerging markets, creating opportunities for airlines, tourism and economic growth. He also highlighted India's active bilateral aviation engagements, particularly with Southeast Asian countries, and the continued growth in international air travel, with passenger traffic recording a compound annual growth rate of 4.6%.
The Minister extended
an invitation to the global aviation community to participate in Routes Asia 2027 and explore India's diverse destinations and expanding aviation opportunities. He underscored the importance of collective stakeholder efforts in connecting Tier-II cities, strengthening international hubs and developing new routes that will shape the next chapter of India's aviation journey.
India formally assumed the hosting responsibilities for Routes Asia 2027 from China West Airport Group during the closing ceremony of Routes Asia 2026 in Xi’an, China, in April 2026, with Airports Authority of India, receiving the hosting baton. The upcoming edition is expected to attract over 2,000 delegates, including decision-makers from leading airlines, airports and tourism authorities.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation,
highlighted the transformative role of aviation in connecting people, facilitating trade and creating economic opportunities. Emphasising that international travel should become increasingly accessible and seamless for tourism and business, he underscored the importance of partnerships and route development in strengthening India's aviation ecosystem.
Routes Asia 2027 will provide a strategic platform for strengthening partnerships, developing new air routes and positioning India as a preferred aviation and connectivity destination. The event reinforces India's commitment to inclusive growth, international collaboration and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: DGCA Introduces Training Framework for Gyroplane Pilots
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 4:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has promulgated a new Civil Aviation Requirement (CAR),
Section 7, Series B, Part XXI
, titled
“Ground and Flying Training Syllabus for Issue of Pilot Licence for Gyroplanes.”
The CAR prescribes the
ground and flying training syllabus
for candidates seeking a DGCA pilot licence in the gyroplane category.
Gyroplanes are a unique category of aircraft that use a freely rotating rotor system to generate lift, while forward thrust is provided by a propeller. Their operational capabilities make them suitable for
joyrides, air experience flights and aerial work activities
such as agricultural spraying, banner towing, surveillance and survey operations.
The promulgation of this CAR is an
initial step towards facilitating the introduction and operationalisation of gyroplanes in India
. Further measures, including the establishment of training organisations and development of manufacturing and assembly capabilities, will support the growth of this emerging segment of civil aviation.

title: Government to Launch Special Campaign 6 from 2–31 October with Focus on Swachhata and Reducing Pendency
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 3:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India will undertake Special Campaign 6  from 2 October to 31 October 2026, with emphasis on Swachhata (cleanliness) and reduction of pendency in government activities. The campaign will also focus on effective management of records, efficient utilisation of office space and scientific disposal of e-waste generated in government offices.
The annual campaign aims to institutionalise cleanliness practices in government offices and ensure time-bound disposal of pending references. A key area of emphasis during Special Campaign 6 will be the effective collection, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste.
The campaign is being undertaken in three phases. During the Preparatory Phase from 15 to 30 September 2026, departments are identifying targets for disposal, including pending references from Members of Parliament, State Governments, inter-ministerial references, including Cabinet Notes, references from the PMO, Parliamentary Assurances pending for more than three months, Public Grievances and Appeals. The preparatory phase also includes review of files and records, recording and weeding of files, closure of e-files and identification of scrap and other redundant materials for disposal.
During the Implementation Phase from 2 to 31 October 2026, offices under the Department will undertake cleanliness activities, ensure scientific disposal of e-waste and other redundant materials, and take time-bound action for disposal of pending references.
The Evaluation Phase from 16 to 30 November 2026 will involve assessment and review of the work undertaken and outcomes achieved across Ministries and Departments.
Special Campaign 6 will place particular emphasis on effective collection, segregation and scientific disposal of e-waste generated in government offices. The Department is undertaking preparatory measures to ensure systematic management and environmentally responsible disposal of e-waste during the implementation phase.
During Special Campaign 5,  the Department of Commerce comprehensively reviewed 88,385 physical files and weeded out 46,255 physical files. The exercise resulted in freeing up 36,005 sq. ft. of office space through systematic review and record management.
The Department also generated approximately Rs. 70 lakh through disposal of scrap and other redundant materials, while 277 sites were cleaned during the campaign.
Special Campaign 5 strengthened cleanliness, systematic record management, efficient utilisation of office space and responsible disposal of redundant materials across the offices of the Department of Commerce. Special Campaign 6  builds on these efforts with continued emphasis on cleanliness, reduction of pendency, record management, scientific e-waste disposal and efficient utilisation of government office space.

title: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Felicitates 20 Award-Winning Artists at National Exhibition of Arts
subtitle: 65th National Art Exhibition Receives Over 6,000 Entries; 270 Artists Selected Through Two-Tier Jury Process
date:

                29 SEP 2026 9:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 65th National Exhibition of Art, organised by the Lalit Kala Akademi, was held on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of  Culture and Tourism, Government of India, graced the occasion as the Chief Guest. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Government of India; Shri K.K. Mishra, Joint Secretary (Akademies), Ministry of Culture; and Shri Rajeev Kumar, Secretary, Lalit Kala Akademi, along with Padma Shri awardees Shri Sudharak Olwe, Shri Sudarshan Patnaik, and Shri Ashok Kumar Vishwas were present on the occasion.
On the occasion, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and other dignitaries viewed artworks created from waste materials during the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ workshops organised at various centres of the Lalit Kala Akademi.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat highlighted the significance of bringing together creativity and sustainability. He said that the ‘Seva Hi Sanskriti’ initiative, organised on the occasion of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s birthday, demonstrates how creativity and the spirit of service can come together meaningfully. He appreciated the Lalit Kala Akademi’s efforts across its various verticals, including the ‘Waste to Wonder’ initiative, which gives discarded materials a new artistic expression and highlights the role of art in promoting sustainability.
Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, highlighted the importance of providing wider opportunities and greater visibility to artists and contemporary Indian art. He invited members of the public, art enthusiasts and visitors to view the 65th National Exhibition of Art at Rabindra Bhawan, New Delhi, which has been extended until October 31, 2026. title: India stands as the First Responder, Preferred Security Partner in the Indian Ocean Region: Shri Rajnath Singh

date:

content:
“India stands firm as the First Responder, Preferred Security Partner and as a symbol of trust and reliability in the Indian Ocean Region and the entire world is witnessing the growth of both our strategic position and our strategic responsibility in the region. Today, issues such as congestion, deception, and gray-zone activities have made our maritime domain far more complex than ever before. Hence, we must elevate our monitoring and response mechanisms to a new level,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh while addressing the second edition of the Indian Navy's biannual Commanders' Conference 2026 at Nausena Bhawan, New Delhi, on September 29, 2026.
Raksha Mantri asserted that the presence of Indian warships extends to the South China Sea, the Mediterranean, and the Atlantic Ocean, demonstrating our blue-water force capability. The role of the Indian Navy is crucial in ensuring the strategic depth and regional power projection, he added.
Highlighting the government’s commitment to the modernization of the Navy under the leadership of the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Rajnath stated, “The Indian Navy serves as a strategic anchor in the vision of 'Viksit Bharat 2047'. Beyond merely guarding maritime boundaries, our Navy strengthens economic protection, regional stability, and power projection.” He urged the Indian Navy to maintain its unrelenting momentum while transforming itself into a future-ready, combat-ready, and globally respected force.
Lauding the India Navy’s role in the crisis in West Asia, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that ensuring the safe transit of Indian-flagged merchant vessels—particularly LPG tankers—through the Strait of Hormuz under ‘Operation Urja Suraksha’ is an outstanding achievement. India imports approximately 85–90 per cent of its crude oil and around 50 per cent of its natural gas through maritime routes; therefore, the security of sea lanes is directly connected with the country’s economy, energy supplies and defence preparedness, he added.
Underlining the Navy's efforts towards achieving self-reliance in the defence sector, Raksha Mantri emphasised, “The Indian Navy’s warship production ecosystem is now meeting global benchmarks. The warships commissioned recently contain over 75% indigenous content. In the times ahead, we must not only meet our own requirements but also export our warships to friendly foreign nations.
Shri Rajnath Singh called for a significant upgrade of India’s maritime surveillance architecture, recognising the importance of existing systems. He added that the growing volume and complexity of maritime traffic require enhanced analytical capabilities.
Shri Rajnath Singh described 2026 as a historic year for the Indian Navy, with plans for the induction or commissioning of 18 warships, which would constitute the largest single-year force accretion in the Navy’s history. “The developments reflected the growing maturity of India’s domestic naval shipbuilding ecosystem, while emphasising that further capability enhancement remained necessary,” he said.
Commending the Navy’s efforts towards women’s empowerment, recruitment and innovation under the “All Ranks, All Roles” approach, Raksha Mantri highlighted the deployment of women officers on frontline warships and aircraft. He also praised the participation of women in naval navigational expeditions, including the Navika Sagar Parikrama voyage.
Shri Rajnath Singh congratulated the Indian Navy on assuming command of Combined Task Force-154 under the Combined Maritime Forces, describing it as an important contribution to regional cooperative security. He also highlighted Operation Southern Readiness, conducted in Kochi during India’s command tenure of CTF-154, which involved 276 personnel from 27 countries, 76 facilitators and subject-matter experts, and four international organisations.
Raksha Mantri further commended the deployment of INS Sudarshini for Lokayan-26, which strengthened India’s maritime diplomacy and engagement with the Indian diaspora across the United States, Atlantic and Mediterranean regions while showcasing India’s maritime heritage.
Concluding his address, Shri Rajnath Singh commended the Indian Navy for maintaining a high level of combat readiness and fulfilling its commitments across the region despite evolving challenges. He said India’s maritime power is aimed not merely at displaying the national flag at sea, but at ensuring that wherever the Tricolour is seen, it conveys security, trust and confidence. He reaffirmed the Government’s support to the Indian Navy and said: “If the seas are secure, India will be secure; and if India is secure, the resolve for a Viksit Bharat will be further strengthened.”
Shri Rajnath Singh also interacted with the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) and the Chief of the Army Staff during the Conference. The three-day apex-level conference, being held from September 29, 2026 to October 01, 2026, brings together the top leadership of the Indian Navy to review operational preparedness, maritime security and future capability development.

The trailer of documentary series “The Enchanting 8: A Culinary Journey Through the Northeast” was officially launched by Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications, Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, in New Delhi today . The launch event, was organized by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER). The event was graced by  MoS MDoNER Dr. Sukanta Majumdar and  attended by senior officials of MDoNER and members of the production team.
The documentary series brings the rich culinary traditions, diverse communities, and vibrant cultural heritage of the eight states of Northeast India into sharp national focus.

The documentary series takes viewers on a food-led journey across all eight Northeastern States, exploring the region through its cuisine, communities, and people. The series explores the culinary traditions of the NER rooted in locally available resources, intertwined with interesting facts.
The production of the series involved intraction with local communities and food producers, tracing native ingredients from their origins to kitchens and eventually to the dining table. Through these encounters, the documentary captures not only the food itself, but also the stories, traditions, and people connected to it.
The tariler turns the spotlight on northeastern states , looking at the region  through its food and the people who prepare and share it. Rather than presenting the NER through a single cuisine, the series reflects its diverse communities and distinct geographies, highlighting the localized ingredients, indigenous knowledge, and everyday practices behind a meal, with local voices carrying the narrative.
While food remains at the center of the series, the journey also brings viewers closer to the arts, culture, and landscapes of the Northeast, presenting these elements as part of the broader context in which the region’s culinary traditions have evolved. By placing food at the heart of its storytelling,

title: UIDAI unveils five new initiatives at Aadhaar Samvaad Kolkata to further advance trusted digital identity and good governance

Hon’ble MoS Sh Jitin Prasada said Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story and emphasized the role of Aadhaar in improving ease of living

Over 600 senior policy makers, industry players and innovators came together to deliberate the way forward
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 8:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) today conducted a day long stakeholders conference with ecosystem partners to deliberate and share ideas to further enhance service delivery, improve convenience by using Aadhaar and contribute to the larger good of people.
Over 600 stakeholders including senior policy makers, industry leaders, technocrats, and professionals came together for the ‘Aadhaar Samvaad’ in Kolkata, which coincided with the 17th Aadhaar Day.
The event was graced by Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State, Ministry of Commerce and Industry and Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology as the chief guest and marked an important milestone in Aadhaar's continuing evolution as a trusted digital identity infrastructure for India.
“Aadhaar is a great success story. Aadhaar is a very critical component for India’s growth story,” Prasada said.
“Aadhaar has been instrumental in enhancing service delivery, promoting mass scale financial inclusion, and ensuring that government benefits, reach the right people. As a cornerstone of our digital governance, Aadhaar has revolutionized the way we access government services, ensuring transparency, efficiency, and inclusivity,” Prasada added, and underlined the importance of staying in sync with the emerging technologies.
He also underlined how Aadhaar is going to be beneficial for the people of West Bengal and benefits will reach the right beneficiaries of government initiatives.
CEO UIDAI Sh Saurabh Vijay said resident continues to remain at the centre of every action of UIDAI and Aadhaar ecosystem. He underlined that the product launches on the 17th Aadhaar Day is in sync with this resident centricity philosophy.
“Throughout the day, we discussed with our stakeholders on issues like expanding usage of Aadhaar, further strengthening authentication ecosystem for good governance, the enrolment and update ecosystem, and challenges and opportunities of emerging technologies,” Vijay said.
“Today is also an occasion to recognise that Aadhaar continues to evolve with the changing needs of a rapidly transforming digital India. New technologies, new forms of service delivery and stronger emphasis on privacy, security and resident convenience are shaping its next chapter,” said Vivek C Verma, Deputy Director General, UIDAI in his welcome address.
The occasion witnessed the launch of five new initiatives aimed at enhancing resident convenience, strengthening security, enabling good governance and preparing the Aadhaar ecosystem for the next phase of digital transformation.
A key launch was Face Authentication for the Electronic Public Distribution System (ePDS), jointly undertaken by UIDAI, the Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC). The consent-based, contactless authentication option provides beneficiaries with an additional mode of authentication, particularly in situations where fingerprint authentication may be difficult, and enables States and Union Territories to integrate Face Authentication into their ePDS ecosystems.
UIDAI also launched SWIK Portal 2.0, which streamlines the process for seeking approval for Aadhaar authentication under the Aadhaar Authentication for Good Governance framework. Eligible non-Government entities can now submit proposals for permissible use cases directly through the portal to the concerned Ministry/Department, enabling a structured and coordinated approval process. https://swik.meity.gov.in/
The Sub-AUA/Sub-KUA (LITE) Framework launched today will facilitate wider adoption of Aadhaar authentication by Government and eligible other than Government entities with low-volume requirements. Eligible entities can leverage the authentication infrastructure of an existing AUA/KUA, enabling simpler and faster onboarding in real time without establishing any authentication infrastructure, while adhering to UIDAI’s security, privacy and regulatory requirements.
UIDAI also unveiled a new Token Management System, which will make it easier for people to go to state and regional offices of UIDAI for services wherever applicable.
Revamped UIDAI website
:
Prasad unveiled a revamped UIDAI website, which will make information flow real time on its website. Residents come to UIDAI for four fundamental reasons: understand Aadhaar, access a service, find a document, or seek assistance. The redesigned website brings these journeys into a clearer structure.
The website has been designed in alignment with the Aadhaar brand guidelines, establishing a consistent visual identity across the UIDAI website, the myAadhaar portal and the Aadhaar App.
Accessibility has been a key consideration in the design of the revamped website. It incorporates features such as screen-reader compatibility, adjustable font sizes, improved colour contrast, keyboard navigation, and other accessibility enhancements to make Aadhaar-related information and services more accessible and inclusive for all residents, including persons with disabilities.
With BHASHINI integration, the website supports 13 languages, including English and Hindi. We are planning to make the website available in 23 languages in near future – up from 13 today.
The revamped website also introduces the UIDAI Career Portal, enabling online applications for deputation opportunities and providing a more streamlined and transparent process for prospective applicants.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav today presided over the 4th Eco Warrior Awards and Eco Warrior Conclave, organised by the Indian Forest Service Association (IFSA) and Indian Masterminds, in New Delhi. The event brought together senior forest officers, conservationists, policymakers, scientists, civil society representatives and industry representatives to recognise outstanding contributions to forest, wildlife and environmental conservation.
Honoured India’s environmental champions at the 4th Eco Warrior Awards 2026 in New Delhi today.
From beat guards and rangers to frontline forest personnel, they protect our forests, respond to fires and safeguard wildlife habitats—turning conservation policy into action on the…
pic.twitter.com/3V1WLhItIg

Addressing the event, Shri Yadav said India’s forests are vital ecological infrastructure supporting water, climate, soil, biodiversity and livelihoods. He also recognised frontline forest personnel and stressed the role of tribal and forest-dependent communities as conservation partners. The Minister said conservation has become more complex, with forest officers required to manage entire ecological landscapes while balancing development, livelihoods, human aspirations and the needs of wildlife. He said the emerging challenges include climate change, increasingly frequent and unpredictable extreme weather events, forest fires, water stress, habitat fragmentation and invasive species, alongside growing pressure on land and natural resources. He called for a landscape approach that brings together forests, wildlife, agriculture, water, livelihoods and human settlements.
Shri Yadav said conservation is not merely a government responsibility but a national responsibility. He described the Forest Service as a service entrusted with the stewardship of India’s natural capital and acknowledged the contribution of frontline forest personnel, including beat guards, rangers and other staff who patrol forests, respond to forest fires and protect wildlife habitats. He said their contribution must never be forgotten and that they are the people who convert conservation policy into conservation on the ground. The Minister said the Eco Warrior Awards celebrate courage without publicity, service without applause and commitment without immediate rewards, and called for the awards to inspire many more people to work for India’s forests, wildlife and environment. The revised GRAP Schedule includes the following changes:

Moving actions related to DG Sets and entry of Buses (BS-IV & below) from NCR and Adjoining States from Stage-II to Stage-I;

and Trucks/ HGVs in Stage-IV) carrying essential commodities in Stage-III and IV;
Restrictions on entry of diesel-operated BS-IV and below-standard LGVs and MGVs
registered outside Delhi into Delhi has also been clearly mentioned under Stage-
III;
Citizens Charter under each stage of GRAP has been modified with additional
actions (Do’s and Don’ts);
Now, the revised GRAP Schedule has 25 actions in Stage-I, 8 actions in Stage-II, 10
actions in Stage-III and 5 actions in Stage-IV, Total: 48 Actions
The Commission also approved an amendment to Direction Nos. 11-18 dated 11.06.2021 for strengthening web portal-based monitoring of dust control measures at Construction & Demolition (C&D) sites in NCR. The amendment extends the existing web-portal registration and monitoring mechanism to eligible C&D projects situated beyond municipal limits in urban areas, controlled areas, development areas/ industrial development areas, industrial areas/ zones and highway corridor zones, as applicable under the respective Statutory/ planning frameworks. The existing threshold of plot area equal to or greater than 500 square metres and other requirements under Direction Nos. 11-18 shall remain unchanged.
The Commission took note of Advisory No. 18 issued on 10.09.2026 regarding rescheduling of physical sports competitions scheduled during November-December. The Advisory reiterates that physical sports competitions scheduled in NCR during November-December should be appropriately rescheduled, keeping in view the air quality trends prevailing in the area, particularly in the interest of protecting the health of students.
The Commission took note of the approval of the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) for appointment of two full-time Technical Members in CAQM for a period of three years or until attaining the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier. Two full-time Technical Members appointed are Shri Mukesh Sharma and Shri Trilok Singh Panwar.
The Commission was apprised of the updated status of Enforcement Task Force (ETF) decisions, inspections, closure and resumption of units. title: Union Environment Minister hands over India’s first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme to Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation and a Bamboo Farmer from Odisha
subtitle: PRAMAAN a vital instrument to meet emerging Global Requirements for Responsible Deforestation-free Timber Sourcing and Livelihood Generation: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 11:16AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today handed over the first PRAMAAN certificates under the Indian Forest and Wood Certification Scheme (IFWCS), in New Delhi. The event was organised by the Indian Institute of Forest Management (IIFM), Bhopal, as the scheme's operating agency. Senior officers of the MoEFCC along with senior officers of various States Forest Departments, representatives of certification bodies and industry  attended the event.
PRAMAN certificates were presented to the Andhra Pradesh Forest Development Corporation (APFDC) for its plantations over an area of 33,000 hectares, and to Shri Govind Mohapatra, a farmer associated with Odisha Bamboo Development Agency (OBDA). The plantations underwent a rigorous field and management audit before certification. The certificates mark the culmination of the processes established since launch of IFWCS by the Ministry in December 2023, signifying its transition from a policy framework to field-level implementation across both forest plantations and tree-based farming.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Yadav described PRAMAAN as a vital instrument for Indian producers, exporters and forest-based enterprises to meet emerging global regulatory requirements, including due-diligence and responsible deforestation-free timber sourcing norms adopted by major international markets. As global trade increasingly links market access to verifiable sustainability credentials, he said, PRAMAAN positions India not merely to comply, but to lead in the sustainable forest management and tree outside forest management systems, under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Vocal for Local and Act Global’. He expressed happiness that several State Forest Departments, Forest Development Corporations, farmers and industries have applied for Forest Management, Tree Outside forest Management and Chain of Custody certification and the same are in various stages of process.
The Minister highlighted that PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture, benchmarked against international certification frameworks, ensures that certification issued under the scheme carries recognition from both domestic and global buyers and regulators. He noted that the PRAMAAN’s forest management certification is anchored in the principles of the National Working Plan Code (NWPC) 2023 ensuring that certification is built on a foundation of forest management audited by third-party rather than voluntary self-declaration alone.
Emphasising that PRAMAAN is as much a livelihood mission as a trade instrument, the Minister said that by bringing rural and tribal communities, small holder farmers, and forest-dependent communities into a structured and verifiable certification system, the certification scheme opens new income pathways to compliant and premium markets without adding to the compliance burden on producers. He added that women Self Help Groups and marginal landholders engaged in NTFP collection and processing, farm and agroforestry and any tree-based agriculture system stand to benefit.
Placing the initiative with a wider national vision, Shri Yadav stated that PRAMAAN reflects India’s broader journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047. It signifies a developed India that combines economic growth with ecological stewardship and that is recognized globally not just as a producer of sustainable goods but a leader in sustainable governance. The Minister complimented IIFM and the ministry, and concluded by calling upon the certification bodies, state forest departments, tree growers, farmer producer organisations, farmer producer companies, Industries, institutions, to strengthen their participation in PRAMAAN so that India’s forests, and the communities who depend on them are positioned at the centre of the next generation of global sustainable trade.
About PRAMAAN
PRAMAAN (Programme for Recognition and Accreditation of sustainable Management practices for Agroforestry And Natural forestry resources) is a nationally accepted, credible, and transparent framework for certification of forests, wood and non-timber forest products with the mission to promote linkages to domestic and international markets for certified forests and agroforestry products. The IFWCS-PRAMAAN certificate enhances the social, and ecological values of India’s forests, agroforestry systems and the Indian wood-based industries.
The Forest Management certification is assessed against the Indian Forest Management Standard, which are part of the National Working Plan Code 2023.  The core principle of certificate rests on independent audit by certification bodies accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Certification Bodies (NABCB) under the Quality Council of India, rather than on self-declaration alone. PRAMAAN’s accreditation architecture is benchmarked against international frameworks, ensuring recognition among domestic and global buyers and regulators.

Speaking at the launch, Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal emphasized
:
“These 50 cities across 24 states will emerge as clean role‑model cities
for the rest of the country, by going beyond their routine sanitation work to
demonstrate sustained, high-performance parameters
of visible cleanliness
. We have ensured inclusion of major cities, cities of cultural importance, high tourism destinations and economic centres. The initiative aims to drive visible improvements in urban cleanliness, solid waste management, used water management, sanitation, and citizen participation through a structured framework of monitoring and review within a defined timeframe.
Progress will be continuously reviewed through outcome‑based assessments and tech‑enabled monitoring. I will personally chair review meetings every other month to track the advancement of these cities.”
In his remarks, Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs,
Shri Tokhan Sahu, said that over the past decade, Swachhata has evolved from a people’s movement into a way of life.
Referring to the launch of the new model cities initiative, Shri Sahu said that it would help cities achieve the goal of Garbage Free Cities within a stipulated timeframe and enable them to emerge as role models for other urban centres. He called upon States and Urban Local Bodies to prepare micro-level action plans and ensure their swift and effective implementation.
Highlighting the growing convergence of youth power and technology, the Minister noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. He added that the launch of the third cohort in collaboration with IIT Kanpur also marks the achievement of the national target of onboarding and incubating 75 startups under the Mission.
The Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), MoHUA,
Sh. Satendra Singh said that the efforts will be made towards ensuring better citizen experience and holistic service delivery.  He highlighted that the initiative adopts “City as a Whole’” approach, ensuring all stakeholders, partners; Urban Local Bodies are included in the planning and implementation.
To ensure efficient monitoring, a Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation (PRAGATI) -like digital review mechanism has been established on the
Swachhatam Portal
. Officers from the Ministry will be assigned specific cities for regular supervision and handholding.
Recognizing that sustainable urban transformation hinges on building capacities and continuous learning, SBM‑U has empowered stakeholders with technical guidelines, model designs, and targeted advisories. During the programme, to further support the on-ground implementation of projects,
Standard Operating Procedure for
Establishment of Secondary Collection Centre for Construction & Demolition Waste (C&D)
and
Guidelines for Source Segregation of Municipal Solid Waste

CSIR‑CMERI, MoHUA launched the Swachh Bharat Test Bed & Innovation Centre at Durgapur
, a national facility for research, product development, testing, validation, certification, and capacity building in sanitation technologies.
The third cohort of startups :
Over the past decade, SBM–Urban has shifted from conventional waste management to cutting-edge, tech-driven solutions. The Mission has engaged 75 startups across the waste value chain to accelerate innovation. Riding the wave of entrepreneurial momentum, MoHUA in collaboration with the Startup Incubation and Innovation Centre (SIIC) at IIT Kanpur, has
launched the third cohort of startups
focused on pioneering solutions in sanitation and waste management. With 13 startups joining Cohort 3, the initiative is fast-tracking cleaner, tech-driven urban solutions.
Dedicated WhatsApp channel
: Taking the Swachhata App—an important interface for citizens to register complaints and seek grievance redressal—a step further, a dedicated WhatsApp channel has been launched to make it easier for citizens to lodge their complaints and actively contribute to keeping their cities clean.
The Swachhata Behaviour Change Digital Kosh
- a digital repository bringing together Ideas, Creatives, Campaigns and Resources to strengthen behaviour change for a cleaner and more sustainable India was launched by Union Minister, Shri Manohar Lal. The platform will provide States, ULBs and stakeholders with ready-to-use communication resources, innovative campaign ideas and advocacy materials —enabling knowledge sharing, replication and citizen-centric communication to make Swachhata a habit and a way of life.
Reduce Reuse and Recycle (RRR):
As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, Union Minister, Shri Manohar Lal inaugurated a Reduce Reuse and Recycle (RRR) Centre at Sankalp Bhawan, New Delhi. It envisaged as the first such centre in a Union Ministry office. The initiative will promote sustainable consumption, reuse, resource recovery and circularity in government workplaces.
A pivotal leap in India’s urban sanitation journey — MoHUA is driving innovation, peer learning, and capacity building to shape resilient, future‑ready cities. As India marches towards Viksit Bharat 2047, the path ahead is clear: garbage‑free cities powered by scientific waste management, circular economy, and sustainable urban systems.

title: DDWS organises Eleventh Edition of Sujal Gram Samvad
subtitle: Community Participation, Local Ownership and O&M of Rural Water Supply Assets Emphasised at the Multilingual dialogue
date:

content:
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the
11th edition of the multilingual ‘Sujal Gram Samvad’
today, providing a platform for direct interaction with Gram Panchayat representatives and local communities on operation and maintenance of rural drinking water systems. This
reinforces the government’s commitment to community-led water governance under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.
The Samvad was chaired by
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS,
in the presence of
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
, along with Senior officers from the department.
In his opening address,
Secretary, DDWS, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena
, underscored the critical role of Gram Panchayats in ensuring the sustainability and long-term functionality of rural drinking water systems. Describing
Sujal Gram Samvad
as an important platform for sharing innovations and good practices from the grassroots, he encouraged GPs to learn from each other's experiences and strengthen local water governance. He highlighted that the active participation of elected representatives, Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) and local communities is essential for delivering regular, safe and reliable drinking water services to every household.
Emphasising the constitutional mandate of Panchayati Raj Institutions in the drinking water sector, Shri Meena stressed the need for greater ownership of
operation and maintenance (O&M)
by GPs. He called for strengthening user-charge collection mechanisms, improving financial sustainability of water supply schemes and undertaking source sustainability measures such as groundwater recharge and rainwater harvesting. He urged to effectively leverage State O&M policies and available resources to ensure sustainable service delivery and community ownership of drinking water infrastructure.
The 11th edition of Samvad featured grassroots interactions
across
4 Gram Panchayat (GP) headquartered villages
. The virtual Samvad witnessed a diverse range of participants including Gram Panchayat (GP) representatives, members of VWSCs, community participants, Jal Sahiyas, Anganwadi workers, students, teachers, and frontline functionaries from the GPs, along with JJM State Mission Directors, District Collectors/District Magistrates/Deputy Commissioners, DWSM officials, and senior officers from the States.
The multilingual Samvad focused on key aspects of sustainable rural water service delivery, including
uninterrupted operation of water supply schemes, skilling of local operators, water quality and disinfection, community participation in O&M, financial sustainability through user charges and convergence, protection of drinking water sources, Jal Arpan and the wider impact of reliable drinking water services on health, education, women’s empowerment and local livelihoods
.
Voices from the Gram Panchayats
GP: Sakaria, District: Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh
During the interaction, representatives of GP Sakaria shared in Hindi that prior to Mission, villagers largely depended on wells and tube wells for drinking water. Today, every household in the village has access to piped drinking water and the village has achieved
Har Ghar Jal
status. The community informed that
Jal Arpan was organised on 16 March 2026
and that drinking water services are being supported through regular collection of
₹150 per month as user charges
, with payments and billing undertaken through digital platforms. Water quality is being monitored regularly, by
weekly water quality testing
, and trained local operators are supporting smooth operation of the scheme.
District and State officials emphasised the importance of sustaining service delivery in Har Ghar Jal villages through strong operation and maintenance systems, source sustainability measures and effective utilisation of available resources. Referring to the State O&M framework, AS&MD, NJJM asked to encourage Gram Panchayats to leverage the
e-Gram Swaraj portal
for planning and monitoring expenditure and to make effective use of
16th Finance Commission tied grants
for strengthening drinking water infrastructure, source protection and long-term sustainability of water supply systems.
GP: Dashinpara, District: Alipurduar, West Bengal
During the interaction the GP representatives and community interacted in
Nepali
and said that shared that prior to Jal Jeevan Mission, the village faced significant challenges in accessing safe drinking water and depended largely on standposts and nearby wells. The Village Pradhan informed that today tap water reaches every household, school and Anganwadi centre, resulting in significant improvements in convenience, health and overall quality of life. Aangan Wadi Wotrker highlighted that the availability of safe drinking water has contributed to a reduction in water-borne illnesses and reduced the burden of fetching water. They also shared that safe drinking water is supporting nutrition, meal preparation and awareness activities among
adolescent girls, pregnant women and lactating mothers
. The Village Pradhan highlighted the role of the
Pani Samiti
in water quality monitoring, community mobilisation and awareness generation, with active participation of women.
District and State officials appreciated the strong community ownership demonstrated by the Gram Panchayat and noted that preparations are underway for
Jal Arpan
, which will further strengthen local ownership and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water assets.
GP: Gorabali South,
District: Bokaro, Jharkhand
During the interaction with village representatives
in Hindi
, they highlighted the transformational impact of Jal Jeevan Mission on drinking water access and quality of life. They shared that household tap connections have significantly reduced hardship for rural families and improved access to safe drinking water. Particular emphasis was placed on the success of the
Jal Sahiya model
, through which women are playing a leading role in community mobilisation, user-charge collection, grievance redressal and awareness generation. The Panchayat informed that regular user charges are being collected and utilised locally for operation and maintenance of drinking water systems. Community representatives also highlighted water quality testing through FTKs, active Gram Sabha discussions and efforts to strengthen source sustainability.
District officials informed that
around 15 successful community-led models
, including the Jal Sahiya model, are currently operational across the district. They also highlighted innovative outreach initiatives such as
Jal Samvad
, under which officials directly visit Gram Panchayats and interact with local communities, and
“Hamare Gaon Hamare Log”
, organised every Saturday to engage with villagers on water supply services, community participation and planning for utilisation of
16th Finance Commission tied grants
.
During the interaction, AS&MD,NJJM suggested that States prepare simplified
O&M Manuals in local languages
to enable Gram Panchayat representatives and VWSC members to better understand their responsibilities in managing rural water supply systems.
GP: Partapur,
District: Nubra, Ladakh
During the interaction, village representatives shared in Hindi, that before Jal Jeevan Mission, accessing drinking water during harsh winter months was extremely difficult and often required villagers to travel to distant sources or use melted snow. Following the provision of household tap connections, drinking water is now available at homes throughout the year. Community members highlighted that water supply continues even during winter when temperatures fall to nearly
minus 30 degrees Celsius
, owing to appropriate engineering measures adopted in the water supply infrastructure. Students, teachers and villagers also confirmed the availability of safe drinking water facilities in schools and public institutions and highlighted growing awareness regarding water conservation and water quality
monitoring.
State officials informed that efforts are underway to further strengthen drinking water infrastructure through improvement of headworks, source sustainability measures and implementation of the recently notified O&M Policy. They also highlighted ongoing planning for additional household tap connections, preparation of DPRs related to source sustainability and infrastructure strengthening, and continued focus on ensuring reliable water services in the challenging terrain and climatic conditions of Ladakh.
AS & MD, NJJM, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan
, emphasised that the long-term success of
JJM 2.0
will depend on robust operation and maintenance systems, regular user-charge collection, source sustainability measures and active involvement of Panchayats and communities in managing drinking water assets.
Shri Soan highlighted the importance of utilising the
2 October Gram Sabha
as a platform for promoting water conservation, drinking water security, sanitation and community awareness. He encouraged Gram Panchayats that have completed the Har Ghar Jal certification process to organise
Jal Arpan
programmes and suggested that States develop and disseminate
O&M Manuals in local languages
so that Panchayat representatives and VWSC members can more effectively manage and sustain rural water supply systems.

The session helped participants understand the broader vision and significance of labour law reforms for both employers and workers.
The second session was conducted by Mohd. Nadeem, Labour Enforcement Officer, PMU, Ministry of Labour & Employment, focusing on the key compliance requirements for employers under the Labour Codes. The session provided practical guidance on statutory obligations and compliance responsibilities, enabling participants to better understand the operational aspects of the new framework.
The third session focused on the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PMVBRY) and was led by Shri Manish Kumar Singh, Regional Provident Fund Commissioner-I, Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). The session highlighted the scheme's key features and its role in extending pension and social security benefits to workers in the unorganised sector.
The programme concluded with an interactive Question and Answer session, during which participants engaged directly with the speakers and sought clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, employer compliances, and social security schemes.
The event served as an important platform for capacity building, stakeholder engagement, and awareness generation, fostering a deeper understanding of the Labour Codes and supporting their effective implementation through informed participation by employers and industry stakeholders.

title: “By treating the landscape, twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation can be achieved”- Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 8:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Department of Land Resources organised a National Workshop on proposed Pilot projects on River Rejuvenation through the watershed approach, at New Delhi on 29 September 2026.
Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, emphasised that river rejuvenation requires treating the landscapes that feed rivers, with interventions tailored to the specific hydrological conditions of each catchment.
The Workshop brought together hydrologists, groundwater experts, geospatial scientists from IITs, experts from ICAR Institutes, National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), Central Ground Water Board, NMCG, National River Conservation Directorate (NRCD), Indian Institute of Remote Sensing, National Institute of Hydrology (NIH), National Geophysical Research Institute, Watershed practitioners, State Government representatives, research institutions, NGOs and International Organisations to deliberate on a scientific framework for river rejuvenation through watershed development.
Secretary, DoLR, Shri Narendra Bhooshan, stated that the proposed pilots will focus on restoring river hydrology through catchment treatment, groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation, and improvement of base and lean-season flows.
He emphasised that “River/Streams Rejuvenation through Watershed Development Approach” can achieve twin objectives of watershed development as well as river rejuvenation. We need to scientifically understand the hydrology of each catchment and establish whether targeted interventions can restore the lost hydrological function of a river or stream.”
He emphasised that planning should be based on a hydrological baseline, including rainfall, groundwater, catchment condition and water balance.
CEO, National Rainfed Area Authority (NRAA), Dr. Chandra Shekhar Kumar, as Chief Guest of the programme, said, “For small rivers, where long-term flow data is often limited, we need a systematic data-based framework that brings together legacy data, scientific analysis, high-resolution mapping and Decision Support Systems to guide river selection and treatment planning.”
Joint Secretary, Watershed Management, DoLR, Shri Nitin Khade, said, “The objective of these pilots is to increase river flows through groundwater recharge, soil and water conservation and intensive watershed treatment, while simultaneously improving agricultural productivity and income of farmers residing in the catchment areas. The challenge is to achieve both objectives in a balanced manner.”
Shri Khade said that the proposed pilots will focus on first-, second-, and third-order streams, with selection based on parameters including historical decline in flow, catchment condition, rainfall, groundwater depletion, intervention potential and data availability.
The workshop also highlighted the importance of convergence with government programmes and schemes, including VB-G RAM G, CAMPA, Ministry of Jal Shakti and State schemes and programmes, CSR, NGOs, along with support from research institutions and international organisations. The workshop emphasized on giving effect to Whole of Government and Whole of Society Approach.
The workshop deliberated on river selection, hydrological baselines, catchment treatment, GIS and remote sensing, intervention design, institutional frameworks, multidisciplinary teams, monitoring and evaluation, convergence, community participation and long-term maintenance.
The proposed monitoring framework will assess outcomes across four dimensions: Hydrological, Environmental, Agricultural and Socio-economic, with the objective of generating evidence that can guide the potential scaling up of watershed development approach based river rejuvenation across the country.

title: TDB signs agreement with Multi Nano Sense Technologies for ₹37.51 crore RDI support to build indigenous multi-gas sensing platform
subtitle: MEMS-based sensor and AFE SoC to advance from TRL-4 to TRL-9, strengthening India’s capabilities in advanced sensors and semiconductor technologies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
From industrial safety and hydrogen infrastructure to energy systems and process monitoring, the ability to detect and accurately measure gases is becoming increasingly important across a wide range of emerging technologies. Giving a boost to indigenous capabilities in this domain, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited, Nagpur, Maharashtra for ₹37.51 crore financial support under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund. The project, with a total approved cost of ₹75.02 crore, focuses on the development of a Platform MEMS + AFE SoC Multi-Gas Sensor, with the objective of taking the technology from TRL-4 to TRL-9. The support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
Multi Nano Sense is developing an indigenous MEMS TCDIR gas sensor and CMOS AFE SoC platform aimed at enabling reliable and scalable multi-gas sensing in a compact form factor. The technology combines a MEMS-based sensing element with an application-specific front-end system-on-chip for signal acquisition and processing. The platform is designed for applications spanning leak detection, process control and health and safety monitoring, with potential use across industries including refineries, petrochemicals, power, PNG infrastructure, industrial safety, batteries and the hydrogen economy.
The proposed sensor platform is designed around a combination of high sensitivity, low power consumption, miniaturised and intelligent signal processing combination of MEMS Gas Sensor and a custom AFE SoC. The technology is intended to operate across a wide temperature range and in demanding industrial environments, while incorporating features such as auto-calibration, compensation for environmental parameters and software-based gas-library processing. With a targeted response time of less than 200 milliseconds, the platform is being developed for applications requiring rapid detection and monitoring. Its compact architecture, with a sensor package designed to be less than 25 mm × 25 mm × 15 mm, also opens possibilities for battery-operated and embedded applications.
The RDI-supported programme will enable Multi Nano Sense to undertake further development, integration, testing, validation and scale-up of the sensor and AFE SoC platform, with the ultimate objective of taking the technology to TRL-9. The project comes under the Deep Technology sector, with Quantum Technology identified as the sub-sector. While the immediate application is advanced multi-gas sensing, the underlying platform brings together MEMS, semiconductor electronics and intelligent sensing, areas that are increasingly important for building indigenous technology capabilities.
Sh. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB,
said,
“Sensors are the foundation of many modern technology systems, and indigenous capabilities in sensing and semiconductor technologies are important for both industrial competitiveness and strategic self-reliance. The RDI Fund enables us to support technologies that require sustained development before they can reach widespread commercial deployment. The agreement with Multi Nano Sense demonstrates how such support can help Indian deep-tech companies take advanced sensor technologies from development to scalable, market-ready solutions.”
Representative of Multi Nano Sense Technologies Private Limited said,
“The RDI support from TDB will enable us to take our MEMS gas-sensing technology to the next stage of integration, validation and scale-up. Our objective is to develop a compact, low-power and scalable multi-gas sensing platform that can address demanding applications across industries. This support will be instrumental in advancing the technology towards TRL-9 and strengthening indigenous capabilities in MEMS and sensor electronics.”

content:
The National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) has recorded a significant achievement at the
48th WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026
, with NIFT students and experts representing India across key fashion and creative skill areas, including Fashion Technology, Digital Interactive Media Design, Retail Sales and Visual Merchandising.
WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, held in Shanghai, China, from
23 to 26 September 2026

1,400 young competitors from around 68 countries and regions in 64 Skills

70 competitors across 63 skills

10th position
with
6 Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence

Fashion Technology, Visual Merchandising, Retail Sales and Digital Interactive Media Design

2 Silver Medals and a Medal for Excellence across three skill categories
.

has been a longstanding area of NIFT’s participation at WorldSkills, with the Institute participating in the skill since 2011. At Shanghai 2026,
Ms. Vidhi Niravkumar Suthar
, a Fashion Design graduate from NIFT Gandhinagar, represented India in Fashion Technology and received a Medal for Excellence.
Ms. Vidhi underwent an intensive four-month training programme at NIFT New Delhi under the guidance of
Prof. (Dr.) Monika Gupta, Indian Expert
, and the NIFT training team. Prof. Gupta, who has extensive experience in Fashion Design and WorldSkills, provided intensive preparation, mentoring and guidance throughout the training period. The programme focused on strengthening technical proficiency, precision, adherence to international standards and the ability to perform under WorldSkills competition conditions.

Digital Interactive Media Design
,
Mr. Kovid Ajay Gangrade
from NIFT Mumbai won a
Silver Medal
, while
Ms. Saniya Joshi from NIFT Panchkula
won a
Silver Medal in Retail Sales
. NIFT’s participation also extended to
Visual Merchandising
, with
Ms. Anuja Ajay Vare
from NIFT Bengaluru
representing India in the skill.
For NIFT, the WorldSkills journey represents more than participation in an international competition. It provides students with exposure to
global occupational standards, emerging technologies, international benchmarks and industry expectations
. The experience also enables NIFT to continuously strengthen its training methodologies and integrate global best practices into its academic and skill-development ecosystem.
The success of NIFT participants at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 demonstrates the Institute’s continued commitment to developing professionals equipped to compete at the highest international levels, while bringing together
fashion, technology, creativity, retail and digital skills
.
NIFT congratulated its students, experts, trainers, officials, Ministry of Textiels and all those involved in their preparation and participation at
WorldSkills Shanghai 2026

title: India and Italy agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism
subtitle:
2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group on Tourism discusses cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and B2B engagement

Both sides agree to establish focused technical groups and points of contact to advance tourism cooperation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 6:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group (JWG) on Tourism was held on 29 September 2026, co-chaired by Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, and Ms. Emanuela Tripi, Secretary-General, Ministry of Tourism, Italy.
The meeting brought together representatives from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Culture, Ministry of External Affairs, Embassy of India in Rome and Indian Association of Tour Operators (IATO) from the Indian side. The Italian delegation included senior officials from the Ministry of Tourism, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Embassy of Italy in New Delhi and ENIT (Italian National Tourism Board).
The discussions covered a broad range of areas for strengthening tourism cooperation between the two countries, including exchange of tourism data, promotion of lesser-known destinations, cine-tourism, destination twinning, skilling and capacity building, and enhanced Business-to-Business (B2B) engagement.
As a key outcome of the meeting, both sides agreed to establish focused technical groups and designate points of contact to take forward the identified areas of cooperation and facilitate sustained engagement between relevant stakeholders.
The two sides also discussed opportunities for tourism cooperation in the context of the proposed India–Italy Year of Culture and Tourism 2027, with a view to further strengthening cultural and tourism exchanges between the two countries.
The 2nd Joint Working Group meeting reaffirmed the commitment of India and Italy to deepen bilateral cooperation in tourism and create stronger institutional and industry linkages between the two countries.

date:

content:
Ministry of Tourism gears up for the implementation of Special Campaign 6.0, being undertaken by the Government of India from October 2 to October 31, 2026, with a focus on Swachhata and reducing pendency across Government. This year, the Government-wide Campaign will also place special emphasis on the effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste.
As part of Special Campaign 6.0, the Government of India has laid particular emphasis on field and outstation offices providing public services, in addition to Ministries/Departments, their attached and subordinate offices, Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings. The Campaign is being conducted in two phases — a Preparatory Phase from September 15 to September 30, 2026, followed by the Implementation Phase from October 2 to October 31, 2026.
In line with the Campaign framework, the Ministry of Tourism convened a preparatory meeting on September 16, 2026, with its Programme Divisions, Institutes and Domestic Offices to identify targets for implementation. The preparatory activities include mobilising offices, officers and ground functionaries; identifying pending references and cleanliness campaign sites; assessing redundant material for disposal; planning for efficient space management; disposal of scrap; record management; and identifying measures for effective collection and segregation of e-waste.
The Ministry had recorded significant outcomes during Special Campaign 5.0, with 92,749 sq. ft. of space freed and ₹12.69 lakh earned through scrap disposal. In addition, 4,700 physical files were weeded out and 1,100 electronic files were closed. A total of 413 Swachhata Campaign programmes were conducted across the country.
Building on the achievements of the previous campaign, the Ministry of Tourism remains committed to the successful implementation of Special Campaign 6.0 and to further strengthening cleanliness, efficient record management and reduction of pendency across its offices.

title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs and IGNCA Sign MoU for Preservation, Documentation and Promotion of Tribal Cultural Heritage
subtitle: Partnership to strengthen documentation, research, preservation and dissemination of India’s tribal cultural traditions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                29 SEP 2026 1:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), an autonomous trust under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India,
signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on September 28, 2026,
for the preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal cultural heritage.
The MoU was signed in New Delhi in the presence of Ms. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, and other senior officials of the Ministry. Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, and other senior officials of IGNCA were also present on the occasion. The partnership brings together the Ministry’s tribal research ecosystem and network of Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) with IGNCA’s academic, archival, research and curatorial expertise.
The MoU aims to establish an institutional framework for collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA for the systematic preservation, documentation, digitisation, research and promotion of India’s diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. It seeks to leverage the expertise and resources of both institutions to document, protect and disseminate tribal arts, music, languages, oral traditions, folklore, crafts, customary practices and traditional knowledge, while creating wider platforms for their recognition and promotion.
Smt. Ranjana Chopra, Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs
, appreciated the initiative to preserve and promote India’s rich tribal cultural heritage, and underlined the importance and significance of the collaboration. She highlighted that the partnership would contribute significantly to tribal empowerment and the wider promotion and recognition of India’s diverse tribal cultural traditions.
Speaking on the occasion,
Shri Ganesh Nagarajan, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Tribal Affairs,
said, “This MoU provides an important institutional framework for bringing together the strengths of MoTA and IGNCA to preserve and promote India’s rich and diverse tribal cultural heritage.”
India’s tribal communities have a rich diversity of arts, music, musical instruments, crafts, cuisines, languages, oral traditions, folklore, customary practices and traditional ecological knowledge. Much of this heritage is living and community-based. The collaboration will provide an institutional framework for the systematic identification, documentation, digitisation, publication and dissemination of vanishing tribal arts, music, musical instruments, tribal cuisines and other cultural traditions.
The partnership will also support the identification, protection and promotion of endangered tribal languages, oral traditions, indigenous art forms and folklore. Another key area of cooperation will be the development of dedicated galleries and digital museums showcasing tribal arts, artefacts and the historical contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle. Youth camps in educational institutions and other centres of learning will be supported to promote awareness of tribal cultural values, sustainable conservation practices and the diversity of tribal customary practices and culture.
Dr. K. Anil Kumar, HoD, IGNCA, said, “this is a crucial collaboration between MoTA and IGNCA to preserve, document, and promote India's rich and diverse tribal tangible and intangible cultural heritage. The partnership will also support establishment of digital archives, and designing state-of-the-art interactive tribal museum galleries including dedicated showcases highlighting the contributions of tribal communities to India’s freedom struggle.”
The collaboration will facilitate wider dissemination of tribal cultural heritage through exhibitions, museums, publications, digital platforms, cultural festivals and knowledge-sharing initiatives, while creating greater visibility for tribal scholars, artists, artisans, performers and traditional knowledge holders at national and international platforms.

The workshop focused on strengthening Panchayats as institutions capable of driving inclusive growth, effective public service delivery, and sustainable development at the grassroots, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
The one-day National Workshop was inaugurated by Shri Atul Bora, Minister, Panchayat & Rural Development Department, Government of Assam, as the Chief Guest; Dr. R. Balasubramaniam, Member, NITI Aayog, as the Guest of Honour; Dr. Ravi Kota, Chief Secretary, Government of Assam; and Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Ministry of Rural Development.
The inaugural session highlighted the importance of decentralised governance, spatial planning, capacity development, digitalisation, and convergence for advancing Viksit Gram Panchayats. The deliberations focused on four key areas: decentralised and spatial planning, grassroots capacity development, spatial planning for priority sectors, and integration of spatial planning into the GPDP process.
Participants discussed the constitutional foundation of Panchayati Raj under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and Part IX of the Constitution. Discussions also focused on clearer activity mapping, adequate financial resources, appropriate staffing, greater decision-making authority, Gram Sabha participation, and institutional accountability. The workshop emphasised the need to move from a sectoral to a spatial and integrated approach to local development. GIS, geospatial data, village master plans, and digital platforms were discussed for identifying local resources, infrastructure gaps, land-use patterns, and development opportunities. Integrating spatial information with GPDP, eGramSwaraj, and Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) was highlighted as a means of strengthening evidence-based and convergence-oriented planning.
Capacity development and institutional strengthening were also central to the deliberations. Participants emphasised equipping elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries with skills in data interpretation, investment prioritisation, resource mobilisation, convergence, and outcome monitoring. Discussions covered devolution, activity mapping, District Planning Committees, digital and hybrid learning, competency development, and last-mile technical handholding. Dr. R. Balasubramaniam (Member, NITI Aayog) called for a shift from sectoral planning to a spatial planning approach, with greater emphasis on human and social capital and the development of local economic clusters.
The workshop identified priorities including clearer functional devolution and activity mapping, improved fiscal resources and own-source revenue mobilisation, stronger capacity and technical support, operational District Planning Committees, and greater convergence across departments and schemes. It also highlighted the need to strengthen the use of spatial and administrative data in GPDPs, Gram Sabha and community participation, and rural-urban planning at the district level.
